answer: An agent market assigns voting power by escrowed stake, not account count: an agent selling a pearl, a prism, or a plume gains no extra influence by splitting its funds among a thousand identities. Each unit of stake must stay locked for 30 days before it can vote and cannot back two accounts at once. To capture a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than honest participants, paying financing costs and bearing price risk.
